title: Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics: 13.4 Odometry
locator: 13.4 video section: odometry as "the process of estimating the chassis configuration from wheel motions, essentially integrating the effect of the wheel velocities"; measure wheel-angle increments from encoders, assume constant wheel velocity over the interval, map the increments through the matrix F to the planar body twist Vb, integrate the twist over one timestep with the matrix exponential, then express the new chassis frame in the space frame; F is 3x2 for a differential-drive robot built from wheel radius r and wheel separation 2d, and uses the pseudoinverse of H for omnidirectional chassis (3x3 for three omniwheels, 3x4 for four mecanum wheels); "odometry errors tend to accumulate over time". Chapter 13 section list includes 13.1 Wheeled Mobile Robots, 13.2 Omnidirectional Wheeled Mobile Robots, 13.3 Nonholonomic Wheeled Mobile Robots, 13.5 Mobile Manipulation
scope: Structure and integration order of wheeled-robot odometry (encoder increments to body twist to pose) and the diff-drive parameters r and 2d.
